question.text: In an experiment to find acceleration due to gravity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>g</mi></mfenced></math> using simple pendulum, time period of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> is measured from time of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn></math> oscillation with a watch of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> resolution. If measured value of length is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> known to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> accuracy. The accuracy in the determination of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi></math> is found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>%</mo></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Time period of oscillation is given by T=2πlg , here, l is length and g is acceleration due to gravity.

From above relation, we have  g=14π2T2l.

Fractional error in g is stated as 

Δgg=2ΔTT+Δll

⇒Δgg×100=2×1100×0.5×100+1 mm10 cm×100

⇒Δgg×100=5100×100=5%

Hence, value of x=5.
